domain: Medieval scriptorium practice and textual criticism of manuscript transmission (stemmatics, colophons, exemplar/copy hierarchies)
axioms: Every copied text drifts; the corpus's failure mode is untracked copying, not wrong content
An index that disagrees with the corpus it indexes routes every reader wrongly
A text without a colophon (version, upstream, last-verified date) cannot be judged living or residue
Cross-references must be maintained like a concordance or knowledge accretes as unreachable folios
Exactly one exemplar must be declared for every duplicated folio; unmarked duplicates are apocrypha
A sync mechanism fed a stale catalog will re-materialize deleted texts over the living corpus
primitives: concordance (index doc: PHILOSOPHY.md, README, upstreams.json, fleet-registry)
palimpsest (doc describing a superseded corpus state)
failure_mode: Cannot judge whether any individual skill is good — a well-transmitted bad text passes every check
Treats the ~/.codex snapshot fleet as purely pathological when it may be a deliberate install cache
Per-skill content review skipped for ~40 plugins beyond doc-vs-actual sampling
Stays at the document layer: blind to runtime behavior, irreversibility, and orchestration mechanics
